To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the MCPS middle school science program is organized in a manner that is responsive to the diverse needs of the county’s students and teachers, (2) the program’s organization is based in part on the objectification of the local and national, and (3) the objectification process is a social and policy-making process.

the objectification process in MCPS has been a successful process for the county in that the county has been able to maintain the diversity of the community while also maintaining the standards of the national curriculum.
the MCPS science curriculum, as implemented in a middle school, is a complex and diverse system that is not well represented in the national science curriculum standards.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the processes of objectification as it relates to the implementation of the national science standards in a diverse school district.
the processes through which the national and the local interact to produce educational outcomes for students.
the processes by which local contexts are shaped by national standards.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the objectification of science standards is not a process that can be easily controlled by a single actor.

the process of objectification is the process by which a community of people, in this case teachers and curriculum developers, come together to create a set of shared meanings that will be used to guide their work.
the process of “objectifying” the curriculum and the students is a process of “objectivity” and “objectification.”
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the objectification of standards is a complex and difficult process that is not well understood.

we have learned a great deal about the processes of curriculum development and teacher training and the ways in which the processes of objectification and standardization are reconciled in diverse local contexts.
the local and the national are in constant tension, and the objectification process is a way of mediating that tension.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the local and the national need to be understood as a process of objectification, rather than as a static relationship.
the process of objectification is not a simple matter of “translation” from the national to the local, or from the local to the national.
the process of objectification is a social and policy issue.
